response: Yes, there is a favorable subset of patients with prostate cancer who develop oligometastases. Oligometastases refer to a limited number of metastatic lesions, typically fewer than 5, that can be targeted with local therapies such as radiation or surgery. In prostate cancer, patients who develop oligometastases tend to have a better prognosis and may experience longer survival rates compared to those with widespread metastatic disease. This subset of patients may benefit from aggressive local treatment of their metastatic lesions, which can potentially improve their outcomes and quality of life.
